title: Love the people you're with
hookLine: fit yourself to your lot and love the people you live among (Meditations 6.39)

cards: The roommate who leaves dishes in the sink. The coworker who talks through every meeting. The brother-in-law with the opinions.
You didn't pick most of them; handed a menu, you might have ordered differently. And there's a quiet daydream: a life where the people around you are easier, wiser, more like you.
Marcus Aurelius didn't choose his people either. He inherited a court, a family and an empire. Near the end of book six, he tells himself what to do with them.

teach.b: Meditations six, thirty-nine, in George Long's translation: "Adapt thyself to the things with which thy lot has been cast: and the men among whom thou hast received thy portion, love them, but do it truly, sincerely."
Two halves: fit yourself to your circumstances, and love your people. Take the word portion. Marcus pictures life as an allotment, a share handed out.

You received these people the way you received your height or your birth year. That can feel like being stuck. Marcus hears it differently: if these are the people you were given, they're the ones your life is for.
Not the imaginary better ones. These.
Then the condition: truly, sincerely. He knew court life, where warmth could be a strategy; in book one he thanks a teacher for showing him the pretense that surrounds power.
So he asks himself for the real thing, which is harder than tolerating people, or performing affection while privately keeping score.

What it isn't: this is no call to stay in harm's way, and nothing in the line asks anyone to accept abuse. It's about the ordinary, annoying, irreplaceable people of a normal life. And notice the order.
Adapt yourself first. The fitting is on his side.
He doesn't wait for them to become lovable; he starts adjusting, and lets love follow.

how: Readers of Marcus often return to 6.39 when daily life with family, housemates or colleagues gets tiresome, using it as a reminder to adjust themselves first and to love the people actually around them.

games.why: Meditations 6.39: adapt yourself to your lot, and love the people among whom you've received your portion, truly and sincerely.

practice: Bring to mind someone you live or work alongside whom you wouldn't have chosen, and set down the list of complaints that wants to start.
Find one true thing about them you could honestly love: a laugh, a kindness, the way they show up. Hold that one thing, and if it's hard, stay with the trying.
